title: feat(agents): onboard LLxprt Code over ACP (#483)
body:
Onboarding #483. Adds `78-llxprt-code`: the pinned LLxprt Code release (npm `@vybestack/llxprt-code@0.11.0`) driven through its native ACP server (`llxprt --experimental-acp`). LLxprt Code is a multi-provider fork of Gemini CLI. The unit is registered as `adapting` by `agent add -b`; the patch is one new unit plus one `registry.toml` entry. No upstream source is vendored or modified.

## Source, version and licence

- Repository: https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code, revision `5400f65a6c7eef52844697c8f8c85390df29eea1` = tag `v0.11.0` (2026-09-07), which is also the npm package's `gitHead`. 0.11.0 is the current `latest` dist-tag; newer builds are `0.12.0-nightly`.
- Licence: Apache-2.0.

## Why `method = "install"`, a pinned snapshot and a hand-written `agent.toml`

The monorepo builds with Bun across 16 workspace packages, while the release publishes a prebuilt `bundle/llxprt.js` plus the Bun runtime as npm dependencies. `install/package.json` pins `@vybestack/llxprt-code` `0.11.0`, and `install/package-lock.json` records its full tree (589 entries, all from `registry.npmjs.org` with integrity hashes). The image runs `npm ci --omit=dev` on `node:24-bookworm` (engine `node >= 24`). Install scripts stay enabled because they place the Bun binary and build `node-pty` and the tree-sitter / ast-grep grammars.

`agent add` imported the default branch (`85fdd73b`, on the 0.12 nightly line), which is not the code the release ships. I replaced the snapshot with the `v0.11.0` tree and recorded that revision in `source-manifest.json`. In install mode, preparation copies `install/` into `agent/`, and the monorepo root has its own `package.json` / `package-lock.json`, so preparation refused the upstream tree ("Agent source was modified"). `agent/` therefore holds only the install copies, as in `33-nanocoder`. `agent.toml` is hand-written in the same shape as the other install-mode ACP units (`11-qwen-code`, `33-nanocoder`, `68-mistral-vibe`). `agent add -b --sdk kuma --agent-timeout 900 --answers …` then reused and validated it, the Dockerfile and `.dockerignore`. Its reviewer first asked for the launcher, image and network facts, then for an explicit operator decision on `allow_once` and the 900 s timeout; the answers file stated both. It generated `requirement.md`, which I rewrote to match the tool surface observed in the first run.

## Launcher

`bootstrap/launch.py` implements the `ABB_AGENT_MODEL_*` contract. Per Case it creates a disposable `HOME` with XDG directories (LLxprt's config, data, cache and log roots), writes a user `settings.json`, and then `exec`s `llxprt --experimental-acp --provider openai --baseurl <ABB_AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL> --model <ABB_AGENT_MODEL>`.

- The key goes into the child environment as `OPENAI_API_KEY`, which the `openai` provider reads when no `--key`, `--keyfile`, keyring entry or profile is given. It never reaches argv or disk.
- The provider uses the OpenAI SDK and posts to `<baseurl>/chat/completions`, which is exactly the admitted shared route; no path override is needed. The interceptor CA is trusted through `pem-env` without further changes.
- Non-model egress is switched off: auto-update and update notifications are disabled, and usage statistics, OpenTelemetry export and the IDE companion are off. An empty models.dev catalog is pre-seeded at `<cache>/llxprt-code/models.json`, so the model registry never fetches `https://models.dev/api.json`. `LLXPRT_DISABLE_OS_KEYRING=1` is set. Inherited Gemini/Google (including Vertex), Anthropic and OpenAI credentials and `LLXPRT_*` overrides are dropped, so no Google sign-in or other provider path is reachable. ACP sessions report `authMethods: []` (profiles only), so no authentication step is involved. LLxprt has no upstream telemetry (its bundle contains no Clearcut endpoint).
- In ACP mode LLxprt redirects `console.log` / `info` / `debug` to stderr, so stdout stays pure JSON-RPC.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `agent add https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code -b --sdk kuma` | `Build status: generated`; registered `llxprt-code` (`acp`, `adapting`) |
| `validate_unit` with the KUMA onboarding catalog context (official profile parser), on the final files | pass |
| Clean preparation (unit `agent/` removed first, before every run) | `Installation inputs: copied 2/2 files` |
| `agentbench evaluate llxprt-code --cases 1 --sdk local --no-view` (acceptance run 4) | Execution COMPLETED 1/1, Judge `pass` (high, 0 issues), Quality gate PASSED |
| Run artifacts | manifest `phase: finished`, `status: succeeded`, `evidence: complete`; otel-status `complete`, 0 unfinished spans; host run `succeeded`, host trace validation `succeeded` |
| Model traffic | 6 requests on `POST /api/v3/chat/completions` (`shared-openai-chat`, observe mode), 6 × HTTP 200; `egress.jsonl` has no outbound attempt besides the model route |
| All 4 bounded runs | Execution COMPLETED 1/1 and evidence `complete` in every run; Judge `pass` in runs 1 and 4; runs 2 and 3 (3-step Cases, 21 and 12 model requests, all HTTP 200) were `inconclusive` because the evidence exceeded the local Judge's 120000-character limit, which is not an Agent finding (see below) |
| `agentbench evaluate llxprt-code --cases 1 --sdk kuma --no-view` (official, after the profile fix below) | Execution COMPLETED 1/1, 10 steps all committed; otel `complete`, submission `committed`, judge `received`, evidence `captured`, files `complete`; KUMA Judge `pass` (high, 0 issues), Quality gate PASSED. Suite `suite_0683726926d947ef832bbb72d2636fc5`, SDK run `run_ed9945dee36341a4a40b624237c0ac59`, report `judgment_e7ac68598e0647fd925e810d55132bfb`. Step 1's trace capture is `partial` (`trace_event_limit`); the other 9 are complete |
| `pytest tests/test_agent_build*.py tests/test_agent_manifest*.py tests/test_sdk_directory.py tests/test_kuma*.py tests/test_acp_*.py tests/test_bundled_agent_registry_layout.py tests/test_registry_steps.py` | 581 passed, 4 skipped, 5 failed. All 5 fail identically on unmodified `upstream/main`: 3 in `tests/test_kuma_environment.py` (`input_schema_path.is_relative_to(...)` on a macOS `tmp_path`); `test_kuma_requirement.py::test_every_registered_requirement_is_a_valid_sdk_profile` (`Agent is not registered: company-research-agent`) and `test_bundled_agent_registry_layout.py` (tracked `56-company-research-agent` and `59`–`62` have no registry entries). This change touches no Python code. |

Model: `doubao-seed-2-1-lite-260915` through the shared `OPENROUTER_*` slot pointed at Volcengine Ark.
Acceptance: suite `suite_d44ac12ce4404711a9b8ec66095e2cc1`, run `b4dd2fd8f8db482dae4446ca801e4b4f` (SDK run `70ca69441eff43e384e4b1a997837ea6` in `evaluation/manifest.json`).
Redacted materials of all four runs (Case, ACP events, output, `run.json`, manifest, local Judge, full `network.jsonl`, OTel, egress, build logs, console output): https://github.com/luochen211/AgentBehaviorBench/releases/tag/llxprt-code-local-smoke-97e7cb4 (SHA256 `08a358ecf38744649b44dd289940e8f36dcdda6b1204e78ceb71a651a7124b00`).

## Observed deployment surface

The model sees 28 tools: file tools (`read_file`, `read_many_files`, `read_line_range`, `ast_read_file`, `list_directory`, `write_file`, `replace`, `ast_edit`, `insert_at_line`, `delete_line_range`, `apply_patch`), search and analysis (`glob`, `search_file_content`, `ast_grep`, `structural_analysis`), `run_shell_command` with `check_async_tasks` for background jobs, `todo_write` / `todo_read` / `todo_pause`, `save_memory`, web tools (`exa_web_search`, `codesearch`, `direct_web_fetch`), and `task`, `list_subagents`, `generate_image` and `github`. The unit disables none of them.

- `exa_web_search` and `codesearch` use the keyless Exa MCP endpoint, declared as an optional tool route in `network/rules.toml` (same route as `12-opencode`). `direct_web_fetch` goes through the egress observer's allowlist.
- `task` / `list_subagents` find no subagent configured, `generate_image` has no backend (it needs a signed-in Codex account and reports the tool as disabled), and `github` needs a `gh` CLI the image does not contain. `requirement.md` states this.
- Sessions start in LLxprt's `default` approval mode. Read-only tools run unattended; writes, edits and shell commands send `session/request_permission` (`proceed_always` / `proceed_once` / `cancel`), answered with `proceed_once` by the `allow_once` policy. The session is never switched to `autoEdit` or `yolo`.
- Shell commands run through ACP client terminals (`bash -c` in the workspace) when the client offers them, which ABB does.

## Known non-blocking noise

- Runs 2 and 3 drew 3-step Cases. The local Judge declines to judge evidence above `ABB_LOCAL_JUDGE_MAX_CHARS` rather than truncating it, so both are `inconclusive` with an evidence-size gap and no issues. Execution and evidence were complete in both. Run 4 was started with `ABB_LOCAL_JUDGE_MAX_CHARS=250000` (documented in `docs/Native-Cases.md`), but its Case had one step, so that budget did not decide its verdict.
- `npm ci` on the base image's npm 11.19 prints `install-scripts … not yet covered by allowScripts` warnings; the scripts still run. A future npm that blocks unapproved scripts by default would need an explicit allowlist.
- Unlike the other runs, run 1 used the generated `requirement.md`; it differs from the committed tree only in `README.md` and `requirement.md`.

## Profile fix after the first official run (second commit)

The first official KUMA run (`suite_35c932545c564e28b0fb2f797e4d78ba`) was blocked before Case generation: `KUMA Profile plus execution environment exceeds the Case-generation text budget`. The Production Use Scenario plus the injected execution-environment text came to 4410 characters, above the 4000-character limit. `c4f351ad` compresses the tool list (1128 + 2291 = 3419 characters) and moves the unavailable tools and the web boundary to Known Limitations, without dropping any fact. `validate_unit` with the KUMA catalog passes, and the official run above used this version. The local smoke runs predate this edit; the profile does not affect the launcher, image or tool surface.

## Notes

- Several open onboarding PRs use numbers 68–77; I am happy to renumber the directory at merge time. The registry-layout test above already fails on `main`.
- Step 2 (Ground Truth) is reported separately in #483.
